title: NFL playoff picture: What does Lions-Bears mean for NFC standings?

But the traditional Thursday games begin with a huge contest in the NFC North, […]
content: (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The annual slate of Thanksgiving games in the NFL has a new addition, with the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game between the Green Bay Packers and the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night at SoFi Stadium, featuring a halftime performance from U2. But the traditional Thursday games begin with a huge contest in the NFC North, when the 8-2 Detroit Lions host the 8-2 Chicago Bears. While it is only Thanksgiving week here in the United States, it is never too early to start thinking about the playoffs. Here is what that game means for the NFC playoff picture. NFC standings Here are the current standings in the NFC: 1. San Francisco 49ers (9-1) 2. Detroit Lions (8-2) 3. New York Giants (6-3-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (5-5) 5. Chicago Bears (8-2) 6. Minnesota Vikings (7-3) 7. Green Bay Packers (6-4) 8. Seattle Seahawks (6-4) 9. Los Angeles Rams (6-4) 10. Dallas Cowboys (5-6) 11. Washington Commanders (3-5-1) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7) 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-7) 14. New Orleans Saints (3-7) 15. Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) 16. Arizona Cardinals (3-8) NFC North standings Here are the standings in the NFC North: 1. Detroit Lions (8-2 overall, 2-0 in division games) 2. Chicago Bears (8-2 overall, 0-2 in division games) 3. Minnesota Vikings (7-3 overall, 3-1 in division games) 4. Green Bay Packers (6-4 overall, 1-3 in division games) Detroit Lions playoff picture As noted above, the Lions currently lead the NFC North, thanks to their 8-2 record and wins over the Packers and the Minnesota Vikings in their two division games. With a win, Detroit would not only maintain control of the division (and move to 3-0 in NFC North games) but they would keep pace with the San Francisco 49ers in the race for the No. 1 seed in the conference. The Lions would also own for the moment a tiebreaker against the Bears, although the two teams meet again later in the season. With a loss, Detroit would fall out of first place in the division — as Chicago would move up — and the Lions would slide down to the No. 5 seed in the conference. Detroit would still stay in the No. 5 spot if the Vikings beat the Atlanta Falcons later this weekend, thanks to the Lions’ win over Minnesota earlier this season. Chicago Bears playoff picture As for the Bears, with a win Chicago would take over the lead in the division, and the No. 2 spot in the NFC playoff standings. Chicago would also control for the moment a head-to-head tiebreaker advantage over the Lions. If Chicago loses, however, the Bears would hold onto the No. 5 spot in the division, at least until Sunday when the Vikings play the Falcons. A Bears loss plus a Vikings win would see Minnesota move up to the No. 5 spot, and the Bears slide back to No. 6. Both teams would be 8-3 in this scenario, but the Bears lost to the Vikings earlier this season. Tiebreaker implications As the moment, Detroit holds the division lead thanks to a 2-0 record in NFC North games. But the winner of Thursday’s game — the first meeting of the year between these two rivals — would hold a head-to-head tiebreaker advantage for the moment. These two teams meet again in Week 17.

title: NFL playoff picture: What does Packers-Rams mean for NFC standings?
summary: Update: With the Rams’ win on Wednesday night, Los Angeles now controls the No. 7 seed in the NFC. The Packers slid down to the No. 9 spot with the loss. content: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Update: With the Rams’ win on Wednesday night, Los Angeles now controls the No. 7 seed in the NFC. The Packers slid down to the No. 9 spot with the loss. The NFL’s annual calendar expansion has a new destination this year. Thanksgiving Eve. For the first time, the league has scheduled a game the night before Thanksgiving, with the Los Angeles Rams hosting the Green Bay Packers at SoFi Stadium on Wednesday night. To help add to the excitement, the NFL has called upon U2 to perform during the halftime break. But this game is important for other reasons. At the moment, the two teams are tied at 6-4, along with the Seattle Seahawks, and if the NFL playoffs began today, the Packers would be in due to a tiebreaker advantage over the Rams and the Seahawks. Which means this game could very well shape the eventual postseason picture. Here is what that game means for the NFC standings. NFC standings Here are the current standings in the NFC: 1. San Francisco 49ers (9-1) 2. Detroit Lions (8-2) 3. New York Giants (6-3-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (5-5) 5. Chicago Bears (8-2) 6. Minnesota Vikings (7-3) 7. Green Bay Packers (6-4) 8. Seattle Seahawks (6-4) 9. Los Angeles Rams (6-4) 10. Dallas Cowboys (5-6) 11. Washington Commanders (3-5-1) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7) 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-7) 14. New Orleans Saints (3-7) 15. Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) 16. Arizona Cardinals (3-8) Green Bay Packers playoff picture For the moment, the Packers are in while the Rams and Seahawks are out. Why? It comes down to tiebreakers. With all three teams at 6-4, under the NFL tiebreaker system we first “eliminate” one of the NFC West teams, either the Rams or the Seahawks. Seattle’s 2-1 record in NFC West games, compared with the Rams’ 1-2 record in division games, knocks out the Rams. Then between the Packers and the Seahawks, Green Bay’s 4-4 record in conference play is enough to give the Packers the edge, as the Seahawks are just 2-3 in conference games. So entering Week 12 the Packers are on the No. 7 line, while Seattle slots in at No. 8 and the Rams sit at No. 9. With a victory, the Packers would hold on to the No. 7 seed, and own a head-to-head advantage over the Rams. However, they could not catch the Minnesota Vikings for the No. 6 spot, even if Minnesota loses to the Atlanta Falcons, as Green Bay lost to Minnesota earlier this season. With a loss, the Packers would drop out of the playoff picture, and the Rams would take their spot at No. 7, at least for the moment. Los Angeles Rams playoff picture As outlined above, the Rams currently sit at No. 9 in the NFC standings, due to the tiebreakers with the Packers and the Seahawks. But with a win, Los Angeles would replace Green Bay as the No. 7 seed in the NFC standings, and could even move up depending on results from Sunday. For example, if the Rams win on Wednesday night, and the Atlanta Falcons beat the Minnesota Vikings, the Rams would move up to No. 6 in the conference, while the Vikings would drop to No. 7. Los Angeles would be 7-4 and the Vikings would also be 7-4, and the Rams would have a 5-2 record in NFC games, compared to 5-3 for Minnesota. If the Rams lose on Wednesday night, however, their chances of making the playoffs take a big hit. They would remain outside the top seven, and the Packers would have a head-to-head tiebreaker advantage should the teams finish tied at the end of the season. Tiebreaker implications The winner of this game will have a head-to-head tiebreaker advantage, which is the first means of breaking a tie for a wild-card spot between teams. NFC North standings Here are the standings in the NFC North: 1. Detroit Lions (8-2 overall, 2-0 in division games) 2. Chicago Bears (8-2 overall, 0-2 in division games) 3. Minnesota Vikings (7-3 overall, 3-1 in division games) 4. Green Bay Packers (6-4 overall, 1-3 in division games, 4-4 in NFC games) NFC West standings 1. San Francisco 49ers (9-1 overall, 3-0 in division games) 2. Seattle Seahawks (6-4 overall, 2-1 in division games) 3. Los Angeles Rams (6-4 overall, 1-2 in division games, 4-2 in NFC games) 4. Arizona Cardinals (3-8 overall, 1-4 in division games)

title: Fantasy football start/sit advice for Week 12 at QB, RB, WR, TE
summary: Welcome to Week 12 of the fantasy football season! This is a tough week for some strong offensive players, especially running backs. content: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 12: Stefon Diggs #3 of the Washington Commanders reacts as he runs off the field against the New York Giants following an NFL football game at MetLife Stadium on November 12, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Week 12 of the fantasy football season! This is a tough week for some strong offensive players, especially running backs. James Cook gets the Chiefs, Christian McCaffrey takes on the Seahawks, Bijan Robinson faces the Vikings, Jonah Coleman heads to Pittsburgh, and Chuba Hubbard will deal with the Bucs top run defense. I’m not going to put any of those fantasy studs as sits, but somebody in that group will likely have a dud. Remember, don’t blindly bench guys who are “sits.” Your fantasy team will dictate if you even can bench a player or not. Bye Weeks None Quarterbacks Start Kirk Cousins, Vikings vs. Falcons Cousins will get a chance to take on one of his former teams, which is good for a “revenge” narrative, but the matchup is much better than facing the Packers and 49ers in his first two games back with the Vikings. Atlanta has given up the eighth-most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks. Over their last two games they’ve given up over 600 yards passing and eight touchdown passes to Joe Burrow and Patrick Mahomes. Caleb Williams, Bears at Lions The Lions have been much better against the pass of late, allowing the ninth-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks over the last five weeks. But, they also didn’t play any top offenses during that stretch. We saw the shell of Baker Mayfield have a decent game against them last week and this game has the highest over-under of the week. Williams is currently fantasy QB13 on a per-game basis. He’s been inconsistent in fantasy, especially with the Bears rushing offense playing well to start the season, but they’ve faltered of late. Add in the Lions strength against the run, and I expect Williams to need to throw the ball a bunch this holiday. Sit Bryce Young, Panthers at Buccaneers The Buccaneers defense is one of the best in the league and despite some positive signs for Young over the last month, he hasn’t come close to his hot start to the season. His inability to deal with the pass rush has hurt him and the Bucs are one of the most blitz happy defenses in the league. When these teams met in Week 7, Young had his worst completion percentage and yardage on the year and threw two interceptions to one touchdown. He also lost a fumble and was sacked five times. Running backs Start Ollie Gordon, Dolphins vs. Jets The Jets have been below average against opposing running backs this season, allowing the ninth-most fantasy points to the position. It is tough to rely on anyone in this Dolphins offense, but if it is going to be anyone, it’s Gordon. His usage remains strong, even with Kyle McCord in at quarterback. He’s seen eight targets in McCord’s two games, along with 31 rushing attempts. Touchdowns might be tough to come by, but with his usage and the god matchup, he should accumulate enough stats to be worth the start. Chris Rodriguez, Jaguars vs. Titans At this point the Titans are truly the worst defense in the league and by a wide margin. The Jaguars are coming off a tough loss to the Giants and will want to set the ship right in an easy matchup. I doubt the team overlooks the Titans after last week’s loss, so there is a real chance they stomp them deep into the earth. Bayshul Tuten has been playing through multiple injuries, so this game would be a good one for him to rest, but even if he does play, I still like Rodriguez. He’s healthier, he will see more work with Tuten not 100%, and the Jags should lead this one throughout, which will keep them in run-first mode. Sit Travis Etienne, Saints at Bengals Etienne finally got back from injury and had a positive offensive day against the Bears last week, as he ran the ball 14 times for 76 yards. He had just one target, which he didn’t catch. He very much appears to be the early down back, which means he’ll need leads to see a full workload. Against the Bengals this week, I do not see that happening. Cincinnati has been decent against the run this year and should be able to score against the Saints, pushing Etienne’s usage down. Kyle Monangai, Bears at Lions I like Monangai a lot and with D’Andre Swift fumbling himself into the dog house last week, I felt good about his chances to see more touches moving forward. Unfortunately, he did not look sharp on his eight carries last week, while Salvon Ahmed had some juice. The Lions are also good against the run, allowing the fifth-fewest fantasy points to the position. I just don’t trust that he’s back to 100% from his turf toe injury just yet. Wide receivers Start KC Concepcion, Browns vs. Raiders Concepcion is a high upside receiver, who can take any pass to the house. Over the last four weeks he has finished as fantasy wide receiver 10, 51, 10, and 30. That WR51 finish came against the Steelers, who sacked DeShaun Watson eight times, but otherwise, he’s shown tremendous upside. Before their bye, against the Texans, he didn’t have a great day as a receiver, but managed a touchdown as a runner. There is no doubt the team wants to get his hands on the ball as much as they can and the Raiders are a team where they can make that happen. They allow the sixth-most fantasy points to wide receivers a Khalil Shakir, Bills at Chiefs Shakir is coming off a strong game, where he caught 5-of-9 targets for 101 yards. He’s also been given five rushing attempts over the last two games. This season Shakir has been a WR3/Flex option without a ton of upside, but this week the Bills face a pass defense that does well against outside receivers, but poorly against slot receivers. On the season, 40% of the wide receiver fantasy points allowed by the Chiefs have come from the slot, which is the highest number in the league. Sure, it’s better to stop the big play outside receivers, but for fantasy, this sets up well for Shakir’s volume. Sit Jalen Coker, Panthers at Buccaneers Coker started so hot this season that it looked like he was going to have a huge year. But, the same can be said for Bryce Young. Young has played a bit better of late, but he also has been spreading the ball around, especially to his tight ends. He just doesn’t have the time in the pocket he once did, making it tough to target his deep threat. Coker has now gone five-straight weeks of not being startle in fantasy and now he faces a great Bucs defense that will make Young get the ball out quickly if at all. Deebo Samuel, 49ers at Seahawks Samuel is still good, which is hard to believe after so many injuries, but he is. The problem this week is that they play a strong Seattle defense on the road and they have more healthy receivers than they’ve had in a long time. With Mike Evans back, plus Christian McCaffrey, Greg Kittle, and Keenan Allen also getting targets, Samuel’s usage will remain low against a Seahawks defense that has allowed the fewest fantasy points to wide receivers this season. Tight Ends Start Chig Okonkwo, Commanders at Cardinals Okonkwo may not have the upside we’d hoped, but he’s still seeing plenty of targets in the Commanders offense. He has 27 receptions on 37 targets over his last six games, but no touchdowns on the season. As long as he’s getting those targets, he should continue to have a decent floor and against a team like the Cardinals, he has upside for more. Arizona hs allowed touchdown receptions to tight ends Travis Kelce (2), Davis Allen, Tyler Higbee, and AJ Barner over their last three games TJ Hockenson, Vikings vs. Falcons Hockenson has become Kirk Cousins’ second option behind Justin Jefferson so far and with Jordan Addison still out, I expect that to continue. The Falcons are middle of the road against tight ends this season at allowing fantasy points this season. It isn’t the greatest matchup, but the way Cousins is targeting Hockenson has me happy to start him against a bad overall defense. Sit Sam LaPorta, Lions vs. Bears The Bears defense has come together after trading for Jeffery Simmons. On the season they’ve allowed the ninth-fewest fantasy points to tight ends and the fourth-fewest receptions. LaPorta hasn’t hit double-digit fantasy points over his last five games, with a high of 7.7 points last week. He’ll need a touchdown to be startable. Kyle Pitts, Falcons at Vikings The Vikings will look to get their defense back on track against the Falcons after Brock Purdy and Kyle Shanahan ripped their blitzes apart. Michael Penix isn’t going to be able to reproduce the 49ers offense anytime soon, so this one could get ugly. I’m still playing Bijan Robinson, but I’d be wary about playing Pitts and even Drake London this week.
